newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian CCB sees shareholders okay CLF alliance.
newsitem.headline: Belgian CCB sees shareholders okay CLF alliance.

text.p: Belgian publicly-owned bank Credit Communal de Belgique/Gemeentekrediet van Belgie (CCB) said on Wednesday it expected its shareholders would approve its planned alliance with French Credit Local de France.
CCB, which specialises in financing local public authorities, is owned by Belgium's municipalities.

"We are currently visiting all our shareholders. Most are very interested in the project. We think that on October 14 our shareholders will react favourably and approve the planned operation," chief executive officer Francois Narmon told a news conference.
The partnership between CCB and CLF will create the 22nd largest bank in Europe and the largest European financial institution specialising in loans to local and regional public authorities.
The two banks are not merging. Their alliance involves setting up a fairly complex holding structure.
The two banks will take cross-holdings in each other's share capital.
A bourse listing is part of the planned alliance. Narmon said the listing of 25 to 30 percent of CCB's shares was scheduled for the first half of November.
CCB and CLF will each create a holding company. The Credit Communal Holding will take a 50 percent stake both in CCB and CLF, which will remain the operational banks.
At the same time the Credit Local Holding will take 50 percent in CCB and 50 percent in CLF.

CCB's current shareholders, Belgium's local and regional authorities, will be grouped into a new Local Authority Holding Company which will take at least 70 percent of Credit Communal Holding. The rest will be floated on the Brussels bourse.
Narmon declined to indicate the value in francs of the planned listing.
Later this month CCB competitor Generale Bank will come to market with a 15 billion franc capital increase.
